correctness.rationale: Fourier–Wigner Laguerre identity and Charlier generating polynomial give the exact positive eigenvalue integrand. Coefficient limits plus Stirling yield the Hermite–Gaussian central envelope, while Poisson Chernoff tails times fixed-order Charlier polynomial growth rule out maximizers at other scales. The q=1 Edgeworth correction changes sign at the two equal leading peaks, and local strict curvature gives integer optimizing degrees c−√(2c)+O(1). Exact and numerical checks in the included runnable checker passed 160 assertions; finite tests do not replace the all-parameter proof. Scope is fixed q,w and a→∞.

value.rationale: A fixed-area annulus translated arbitrarily far outward is a natural localization regime different from enlarged regions. For each Hermite window the theorem gives a sharp exact leading concentration constant and identifies all optimal signal-degree bands. For the first excited window it resolves an otherwise degenerate choice using an explicit skewness term, giving a useful optimal-frequency design rule. These conclusions are neither isolated table values nor merely restatements of known radial diagonalization.
